Ulster University offers undergraduate and postgraduate study across Northern Ireland, with selected branch-campus programmes in London, Birmingham and Manchester.

For international students planning for 2027, one detail matters immediately. January 2027 belongs to the 2026/27 academic year, while September 2027 falls within 2027/28. That affects tuition fees, course availability and financial planning.

If you are still comparing destinations, this guide to planning UK study gives the wider picture.

Popular Ulster University courses for international students

Ulster offers courses across business, computing, engineering, health, accounting, law, marketing, tourism and other career-focused areas.

The right course depends on four things: your previous qualification, target career, budget and preferred campus.

Course names can look similar while the content is quite different.

For example, a general International Business course and a route that includes Data Analytics may share management modules, but the second option can involve more quantitative work and lead to a different graduate profile.

If you have not chosen a subject yet, this comparison of career-focused UK study areas can help narrow the options.

Undergraduate courses

September 2027 applicants can find undergraduate study in areas such as:

  • Accounting and Finance
  • Computer Science and Computing
  • Engineering
  • Biomedical Science
  • Nursing
  • Architecture and the built environment
  • Business and Management
  • Marketing
  • Law
  • Tourism and Hospitality

Some degrees include a placement or sandwich year.

That increases the course length and adds a placement-year fee, but it can also give you relevant workplace experience before graduation. A shorter degree is therefore not automatically the better-value option.

Where UCAS is required, follow the route shown on the individual course page. This walkthrough of the UK undergraduate application process explains how the system works.

Postgraduate courses

January 2027 is particularly relevant for postgraduate applicants.

Ulster currently promotes more than 25 Masters programmes starting in January at its Northern Ireland campuses. Subject areas include Business and Management, Computing, Engineering and the Built Environment, Law and English, and Nursing and Health Sciences.

September 2027 gives students a wider postgraduate cycle. Common options include Management, International Business, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Public Health, Marketing, Human Resource Management and Pharmaceutical Sciences.

Some Masters programmes include Advanced Practice or an extended format. These can run longer and use a different fee structure, so compare course duration, credit requirements and placement content before choosing.

Students comparing business degrees may also find this guide to choosing between UK postgraduate business routes useful.

Ulster University tuition fees for international students in 2027

January 2027 uses the 2026/27 academic-year context. September 2027 uses 2027/28 fees.

Before building your final budget, check the university's latest international fee schedule.

January 2027 tuition fees

January 2027 falls within the 2026/27 academic year.

The standard international Masters fee for 2026/27 is £18,310, while some specialist courses have higher fees.

Here's the part that is easy to miss.

Many programmes beginning in January continue into the 2027/28 academic year. Ulster states that modules undertaken during 2027/28 can be charged at 2027/28 prices.

That means a January applicant should check the complete course structure rather than assuming the initial headline fee applies unchanged to every module.

The course, campus and intake all matter. Check the branch-campus fee and date information before relying on a quoted figure.

Ulster University acceptance rate

Ulster University does not publish an official university-wide acceptance rate.

Third-party estimates vary, so they should not be treated as an admissions benchmark. Your actual chances depend on your chosen course, academic profile, English evidence, additional selection requirements and available places.

A student applying to a general business programme, for example, may go through a different selection process from someone applying to Nursing, Medicine, Architecture or another professionally regulated course.

There is another point students sometimes overlook. Meeting the published academic requirement does not guarantee a place if a programme reaches capacity.

Instead of relying on an unofficial percentage, compare your profile with the university's country and programme entry guidance.

Ulster University entry requirements for international students

There is no single entry requirement for every applicant.

Ulster assesses students according to their country, qualification, level of study and individual programme.

Applicants commonly need:

  • Academic certificates and transcripts
  • A valid passport
  • English language evidence
  • A supporting statement where required
  • Academic or professional references where required
  • A CV for selected postgraduate courses
  • Work-experience evidence for relevant programmes
  • A portfolio, test or interview for selected courses

Undergraduate programmes can require specific subjects or grades above the university's general minimum.

For postgraduate study, many programmes ask for the equivalent of a UK honours degree. The required classification and subject background depend on the course.

Does Ulster University accept HND for Masters?

An HND does not automatically qualify a student for every Masters programme.

Ulster assesses qualifications against the entry requirements of the chosen course and the applicant's country. Some alternative or extended routes may consider a broader academic profile.

HND holders should therefore check the individual programme before assuming they are eligible.

If your course requires a written statement, this guide to preparing a stronger motivation letter can help.

Ulster University English language requirements

For many programmes, Ulster's standard English requirement is IELTS Academic 6.0 overall with no band below 5.5.

Some courses require a higher score.

For courses using the standard IELTS 6.0 level, current equivalents include:

Test

Current published requirement

IELTS Academic

6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

PTE Academic

59 overall, minimum 59 in each part

Duolingo English Test

110 overall, no subscore below 100

Ulster accepts the Duolingo English Test for eligible courses when the test meets its published conditions. DET results from before July 2024 are not accepted under the current guidance.

The university also accepts IELTS Academic Online and IELTS One Skill Retake.

PTE Academic Online is not currently accepted.

One common mistake is to assume that "IELTS not required" means no English evidence is needed. Usually, it means another accepted qualification may meet the requirement.

Before paying for a test, review Ulster's current English-language evidence table.

You can also compare English-test routes used by UK universities.

January 2027 or September 2027 intake?

The better intake depends on your course and how ready you are.

January 2027

January may suit you if:

  • Your preferred Masters is available
  • Your degree documents are complete
  • You already meet or are close to meeting the English requirement
  • You do not need the wider September course choice

Ulster currently promotes more than 25 January-start Masters at its Northern Ireland campuses.

September 2027

September may be better if:

  • You are applying for undergraduate study
  • Your preferred programme does not start in January
  • You want a wider choice
  • You still need an English test
  • You need more time to arrange funds

Think about it this way.

A student who already holds a bachelor's degree, has IELTS 6.5 and has funds ready may gain little from waiting if the right Masters starts in January.

Another student who still needs an English test and wants a September-only course is usually better off preparing properly rather than rushing an earlier intake.

You can compare other UK January options or review the main September admissions cycle.

Ulster University application deadlines for 2027

There is no single deadline for every Ulster programme.

For undergraduate applications submitted through UCAS, the equal-consideration deadline for most 2027 courses is 13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time.

Some course groups use an earlier deadline.

International and postgraduate applicants should follow the date and application route shown on their exact course page because direct and branch-campus deadlines can differ.

Use the university's current application guidance before submitting.

Ulster University scholarships for international students

Ulster currently confirms scholarship support for eligible international applicants starting in January 2027 at its Northern Ireland campuses.

Global Excellence Scholarship

For eligible postgraduate students, the published award is £5,000.

For eligible undergraduate students, it provides:

  • £5,000 in Year 1
  • £3,000 per academic year in Years 2 to 4

Country Scholarships can also be available, with the amount depending on nationality.

International applicants are automatically assessed for these awards, so no separate scholarship application is required.

There is an important timing point.

The currently published Global Excellence eligibility covers programmes starting in September 2026 or January 2027. Students targeting September 2027 should check again instead of assuming the same award will continue unchanged.

January 2027 payment plan

For full-time postgraduate students starting in January 2027, Ulster states that students who cannot pay the full tuition fee must pay at least 50% of the total programme cost at registration, including the deposit.

The remaining balance can then be paid in two equal instalments:

  • 1 April
  • 1 July

Before transferring money, review the university's current self-funded payment instructions.

Ulster University campuses and locations

Ulster's main Northern Ireland locations are Belfast, Coleraine and Derry~Londonderry.

The university also operates specialist facilities at Jordanstown Sports Village, while selected courses are available through branch campuses in London, Birmingham and Manchester.

Do not choose a campus first and then force a course to fit it.

The course, accreditation and teaching location should usually come first.

Ulster University ranking and employability

Ulster University is ranked =595 in the QS World University Rankings 2027.

Rankings can help with comparison, but they should not outweigh course-specific factors such as accreditation, modules, placement opportunities and professional relevance.

Ulster reports that 97% of students progress to a career or further study.

It also reports more than 2,500 work placements each year, with placement opportunities available across many programmes.

A more useful question is whether your chosen course develops the skills and experience needed for the career you want.

You can review Ulster's career and placement support before comparing similar degrees.

Working while studying

How to apply to Ulster University

The safest process is to start from the individual course page.

  1. Choose the course, campus and intake.
  2. Check academic requirements.
  3. Confirm the English requirement.
  4. Review the applicable tuition fee.
  5. Check scholarship eligibility.
  6. Apply through the route shown on the course page.
  7. Upload the required documents.
  8. Meet any conditions attached to your offer.
  9. Pay the required deposit where applicable.
  10. Arrange accommodation, travel and enrolment.

Ulster may also request qualification verification if supporting documents cannot be verified directly.

If you want your shortlist or application plan checked before submission, you can discuss your options with a study adviser.

Is Ulster University a good choice for international students?

Ulster can be a strong option for students who want career-focused programmes, Northern Ireland study locations, selected January Masters routes and placement opportunities.

It may be less suitable if your preferred programme is not available at the campus you want, another university offers stronger accreditation for your target profession, or your budget relies heavily on income from part-time work.

A strong university decision usually becomes clear across six areas: course, campus, fee, entry requirements, intake and career fit.

Get those six right before accepting an offer.

Conclusion

Ulster University gives international students a broad mix of undergraduate and postgraduate options for 2027, but January and September applicants need to plan differently.

The best intake is not necessarily the earliest one. It is the one where your course is available and your application is financially and academically ready.

If you need help comparing your options, you can review your study plan with BHE UNI.

Frequently asked questions

What are the best Ulster University courses for international students in 2027?

Popular areas include Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Business and Management, Accounting, Engineering, Nursing, Public Health, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Marketing, Tourism and Hospitality. The best course depends on your academic background, budget and career goal.

How much are Ulster University tuition fees for international students in 2027?

For September 2027, the standard 2027/28 undergraduate fee is £18,030 per year and the standard taught Masters fee is £18,880. Postgraduate Research is £19,630, while selected specialist programmes can cost more.

What is the Ulster University acceptance rate?

Ulster University does not publish an official university-wide acceptance rate. Third-party estimates vary and should not be treated as an admissions benchmark. Your chances depend on the programme, qualifications, English evidence, additional selection requirements and available places.

What are Ulster University entry requirements for international students?

Requirements vary by country and programme. Applicants commonly need academic certificates and transcripts, English-language evidence and any course-specific documents such as references, a CV, portfolio, interview or work-experience evidence.

Does Ulster University accept HND for Masters?

An HND does not automatically meet the requirements for every Masters course. Eligibility depends on the programme, qualification equivalency and the applicant's wider academic profile.

Does Ulster University accept Duolingo?

Yes, for eligible courses. For programmes using the standard IELTS 6.0 requirement, the current published Duolingo requirement is 110 overall with no subscore below 100. Ulster does not accept DET results from before July 2024 under its current guidance.

What are Ulster University PTE requirements?

For courses requiring IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, the current PTE Academic equivalent is 59 overall with at least 59 in each part. PTE Academic Online is not currently accepted.

Does Ulster University have a January 2027 intake?

Yes. Ulster currently promotes more than 25 Masters programmes starting in January 2027 at its Northern Ireland campuses.

Should I choose January 2027 or September 2027?

January can suit postgraduate applicants whose preferred programme is available and whose documents, English evidence and finances are ready. September usually offers a wider course cycle and more preparation time.

How much are Ulster University Birmingham fees for international students?

Fees vary by programme and academic year. For 2026/27, MSc International Business is listed at £14,550 in Birmingham. September 2027 applicants should check the updated course-specific rate.

How much are Ulster University London fees for international students?

For 2026/27, MSc International Business is listed at £16,200 in London. Other courses can have different rates, so students should verify their specific programme.

What is the Ulster University employability rate?

Ulster reports that 97% of students progress to a career or further study and that it awards more than 2,500 work placements each year. These are university-wide figures.
